forecast-period.text: A trough will continue to move over southeastern parts of the state today. A cold front will clip the far southeast this afternoon and evening before a high pressure system moves over the Bight from Wednesday. The high will extend a ridge across the state, as it slowly moves east into NSW by Saturday.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Morning frost patches about the pastoral districts. Showers about the Agricultural Area and parts of the west coast, extending into the south of the Pastoral districts during the day before contracting to southern coastal districts by the evening. Isolated gusty thunderstorms are possible about southern coastal fringe of the Lower South East in the evening. Small hail is also possible with showers in the southeast. Maximum temperatures below average in the west, near average elsewhere. North to northwesterly winds in the northeast, shifting west to southwesterly throughout during the day. Winds fresh and gusty at times about the southeast, easing the evening.

Possible morning fog patches in the southwest. Isolated light showers about the Agricultural Area and west coast, particularly about windward facing coasts and ranges. Small hail is possible with showers in the far southeast. Maximum temperatures below average. Southeast to southwesterly winds, tending easterly in the west.

Morning fog and frost about Eyre Peninsula, and on and east of the ranges. Chance of isolated light showers about the Southern Agricultural Area. Maximum temperatures below average. Variable winds across the southeast, tending northeast to southeasterly winds in the north.

text.p: Possible morning frost inland and morning fog about the Agricultural Area on and east of the ranges. Possible light morning showers about southern coasts and ranges. Maximum temperatures below average. Northeast to southeasterly winds.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Friday: Generally, less than 3 mm about the Northern Agricultural Area and south of the Pastoral districts, with falls between 2 to 10 mm about the Southern Agricultural Area. Isolated falls of 5 to 15 mm possible about the Lower South East.
